entries.note: VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR: usage ColorAttachment | TransferDst | Sampled, one array layer, identity pre-transform, opaque composite alpha, clipped, no old swapchain. The preview falls back to the current transform and the first supported alpha mode when identity or opaque is not offered, and always uses exclusive sharing (one family).
Swapchain image wrappers: createHandleForNativeTexture(VK_Image) with initialState Present, keepInitialState, isRenderTarget.

The engine clamps its back-buffer size into the surface's range. The preview uses currentExtent, takes the passed window size only when currentExtent is 0xFFFFFFFF, and makes no swapchain for 0×0 (§3.1).

The engine's r_swapInterval / r_vkPreferFastSync choice among MAILBOX, IMMEDIATE, FIFO_RELAXED and FIFO. The preview uses MAILBOX if offered, else FIFO, and FIFO when forced (D48, R5.4); IMMEDIATE only if LP0 measures FIFO's present blocking beyond a bound.

The engine acquires with an infinite timeout and asserts on the result, and cycles one semaphore per image for both acquire and present. The preview acquires with a 50 ms timeout (D48) through the vk::Result overloads, skips on TIMEOUT or NOT_READY, posts SwapchainOutOfDate on OUT_OF_DATE or SUBOPTIMAL, and keeps acquire semaphores per frame in flight and present semaphores per image, all owned by the swapchain generation.

The engine's single frame event query, waited per NUM_FRAME_DATA. The preview keeps a ring of kFramesInFlight event queries and waits on frame N - 2's before recording frame N (D35). The wait polls the event query and ends on a stop or a park, where NVRHI's waitEventQuery would wait without a bound (review L2.1).

Optional device extensions and features the preview does not need: VK_EXT_debug_marker (debug utils replaces it), VK_EXT_descriptor_indexing (its features are core 1.2 and enabled through VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features), VK_KHR_buffer_device_address and bufferDeviceAddress (ray tracing only; the engine notes it 'only makes problems'), VK_NV_mesh_shader, VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate and its features, VK_KHR_format_feature_flags2, VK_GOOGLE_display_timing and hostQueryReset (Optick), the ray-tracing extensions, the macOS portability subset.

Instance extensions: VK_KHR_get_physical_device_properties2 (core since 1.1; the instance is 1.2), VK_EXT_sampler_filter_minmax (listed by the engine as an instance extension, but it is a device extension and its feature is never enabled), VK_EXT_debug_report and its callback (replaced by VK_EXT_debug_utils, which Qt adds for its debug output redirect when the session validates; the tests' own instance asks for it itself). Qt adds the surface extensions.
The VK_LAYER_MESSAGE_ID_FILTER environment variable: a process-wide setting; LP0 creates no pipelines, whose warnings it filters. Revisit when pipelines arrive (LP2).
The D24S8 format probe, the VMA allocator, the push-constant size and Optick's GPU init: not used by LP0. The push-constant size and the depth format come with the passes (LP2, C2).
Compute and transfer queues: the preview submits everything, uploads included, on the graphics queue (S35).

The engine's destruction order (waitIdle, semaphores, swapchain, device handle, VkDevice, surface, instance) never collects NVRHI garbage. The preview follows §3.1's teardown steps instead: release handles, waitForIdle, runGarbageCollection (skipped when lost), wrappers, vkDestroySwapchainKHR, semaphores, the NVRHI device with its last Release() count, then the VkDevice; the surface and the instance belong to Qt.

Before anything can parse it, every material decl whose text can make more than 256 slots is made the default material, with the engine's warning, and its lookup fails with that reason. The bound comes from the copied idLexer's tokens with DECL_LEXER_FLAGS (forEachDeclToken, the tokens idMaterial::Parse reads): after the first "{" (SkipUntilString), every token equal to "{" counts 1 and every stage shortcut keyword 2, whatever its type and wherever it stands. ParseMaterial calls ParseStage only for such a token, once per token. A stage is diffuse only through ParseBlend's diffusemap or basecolormap: in a "{" block that is a token of the material's text, counted 2, which pays for the block's coverage slot; a shortcut's stage is parsed from synthesised text holding its image name without the quotes (AppendToken), so diffusemap "_white alphaTest 0.5" makes two slots that its second count pays for. AddImplicitStages adds at most one stage, below the limit, without an alpha test. So the bound is never below the slots the engine writes; it is above them where such a token is an argument, a block's own keyword or text after a parse error (M-ID-DIFF-03). entries.note: LP1c.1 (C8, D23, A3): the cache file through the C8 search (OpenFileRead: loose, then .pk4, then .resources), read and time-tested as LoadFromGeneratedFile; when that fails and resource files are in use, the BFHACK name the same way; a loaded cache is used when its colour format, format (RGBA8 for RGB565, R11G11B10F for BC6H) and texture type equal DeriveOpts'. Where the engine would binarize, the preview reports Missing (no file) or Stale (a file it would not use, with the engine's binarize reason) for LP1c.2's fallback; it never writes. The editor image is never asked (C8)

LP1c.1: every count and size is checked before it is used: a header shorter than 36 bytes (the engine reads it as it is), a negative or impossible level count, a negative data size, an odd RGB565 level (the engine's in-place expansion reads misaligned pairs) or a level cut short fails the read, where the engine reads garbage or past the end; the preview then reports the cache Stale. A block-compressed level keeps its stored bytes: the engine pads its own allocation to NVRHI's row pitch times the rows, which LP2 does at upload LP1c fix (S3.5): the header's sides must be 1 to 16384 and its level count 1 to the levels its larger side halves into; each level record must be the one the engine's binarizer writes at its place (record k of a 2D image is level k, side 0; of a cube level k / 6, side k % 6: level-major), of that level's size (max(1, side >> level); a block format's cube level below 4 padded to 4) and with at least the bytes its format needs for that size (whole 4 x 4 blocks for DXT1, DXT5, BC6H, BC7, ETC1; the engine asserts dataSize >= w * h * bpp / 8); else the cache is Stale with the reason and never Ready, so LP2 never uploads a shape its header does not state

LP1c.1: the preview mirrors the engine as SinkBroom's users build it: STANDALONE off (TD_LIGHT is RGB565; a STANDALONE build stores RGBA8, which the match accepts for RGB565 anyway) and com_productionMode 0 (the time call runs and the staleness test applies; production mode trusts any cache)

entries.note: LP1c.1: an image's slot is read once per session, when it is first asked for, and kept across material reloads (it does not depend on the decls); the engine reads it at every image load. LP1c.2 (LP1c.1's follow-up 5): the poll re-reads a slot when a loose file it was read from or its time call found changes (its time, size or change stamp; M-IMG-DIFF-06), so a saved source or a new cache is seen; a file in a container, a file that appears where none was, or a reload's new containers are seen after a restart of the session LP1c fix (S2.5, S3.4): the time call's probes that missed are recorded too (the .tga default, the png/tga/jpg/exr/hdr loop, the _rmao sibling; not the cache names), so a texture written after its material is seen at the next poll, and the slot read again; a reload drops every slot (M-IMG-DIFF-09). New containers, and caches the engine writes into one, are seen through a reload (materialCollectionsDidChange) or a new session LP1c fix round 2 (X.3, X.5): a slot keeps every file it was read from or looked for, container entries and the cache names a read missed included, and the poll compares them by kind, container and time (and size and change stamp for a loose file): a loose file over a container entry, or a cache the engine writes later as a loose file, is seen at the next poll, a new container's at the next reload. The C21 sizes keep every file alike LP1c fix round 3 (Y.2): a container entry's probe carries the container file's own change stamp and size from when its table was read (not compared by ==), so a container rebuilt in place reads as changed after a reload and its slots are dropped

A .proc that does not parse counts as none and the .bproc stands in, with the version gate the engine applies (a version-1 or 2 file only without any .proc)

§3.7 (LP1c.1), not in the engine: the area counts of the files that exist must agree: the grid names each area once and as many areas as the tree has, every SH probe's area is -1 or below the count; a mismatch drops the grid and the probes (no-bake behaviour) with the reason, and keeps the tree (the newest dmap's). A file that does not parse (dmap or a bake writing it) counts as no file, where the engine stops the map load at its Error; the parse thread probes the files of every bake it holds each poll and reads a changed bake again, so it is retried on the next change. A binary grid that does not parse falls back to the text LP1c fix (S3.12): an SH probe outside the area range drops the probes alone (shProbesError), not the grid; LP1c fix (S3 Low): a text grid's points are appended as they parse, so a count the text cannot hold allocates nothing; LP1c fix (S3.13): a bake read that throws answers its ticket with a slot that says why; K29 (LP4.3): SinkBroom's own rule, the engine cross-checks nothing: it keeps what matches by index and defaults the rest silently, and a grid area at or past the area count is a fatal load error; the preview drops the grid and the probes with the reason on the status line (bake: dropped (<reason>), D90), and the tree stays in use (K16); the grid table is then empty and every surface takes the probe path (black without probes)

the colour map is not skipped: the decoder reads the colour map's bytes as pixels, and the image data past them runs off the buffer's end. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the colour map type is 0 (tgaProblem)

the size check uses pixel_size >> 3; the uncompressed loop reports 298 per pixel without advancing, the RLE loop 337/389 per packet, so the picture keeps uninitialised or stale pixels. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the pixel size is 24 or 32, or 8, 24 or 32 for a grey image (tgaProblem)

the decoder reads numBytes from a buffer that holds fewer: it reads past the end of the file's buffer. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the declared size fits the bytes after the header and comment (tgaProblem)

reported once per pixel; neither the read nor the write pointer moves, so the pixel stays uninitialised and the rest of the row shifts. the run writes the previous packet's colour packetSize times. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the run-length decoder only meets 24 or 32 bits (tgaProblem)

the pixel is not written but counted, so it stays uninitialised. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the run-length decoder only meets 24 or 32 bits (tgaProblem)

frees tinyexr's message and returns without a picture; R_LoadImage tries the other extensions. The file's buffer is not freed on this path (M-IMG-DEFECT-01). entries.note: LP1c.2 (D51, R5.3, C17): every file a copied loader reads is validated outside the copied code before the loader sees it. The file system, between beginImageReads and endImageReads (MaterialDecls::loadImagePixels), reads it through the source's readGameFile and hands the loader nothing (-1, no buffer, FILE_NOT_FOUND_TIMESTAMP) for a file that fails, keeping the refusal once per path; a stop reads every image file as missing, never as an empty buffer. The checks follow each loader's reads: TGA - the 18-byte header, type 2, 3 or 10, no colour map, 24 or 32 bits (8 too for grey), the declared size of an uncompressed image against the bytes after the header and comment, the RLE packets walked as the decoder walks them up to the last pixel; PNG - stb_image's header rules (signature, a 13-byte IHDR first, depth 1/2/4/8/16, colour type 0/2/3/4/6, 16-bit palettes refused, methods 0, interlace 0 or 1, PLTE before IDAT for a palette, unknown critical chunks), every chunk inside the file up to IEND, and the declared pixels within 1032 bytes per IDAT byte (deflate's limit); JPG - SOI, every marker segment inside the file, a baseline or progressive 8-bit frame of 1, 3 or 4 components with sampling 1-4 and tables 0-3, each scan's entropy-coded bytes walked to the next marker, EOI reached, and at most 8 blocks per scan byte (a block of the finest component costs at least one Huffman bit); EXR - tinyexr's ParseEXRVersionFromMemory and ParseEXRHeaderFromMemory, single part and not deep, one channel or R, G and B (what LoadEXRFromMemory needs), for a scanline image the offset table and every block inside the file; HDR - stb_image's identifier, header with FORMAT=32-bit_rle_rgbe, '-Y h +X w' line, and every pixel byte stb_image reads (flat, run-length scanlines, the flat fallback), so stb_image always decodes it to three channels. Every size: at least 1, at most 16384 a side and 8192 x 8192 in all (M-IMG-DIFF-04). An empty file fails. Tested with truncated, 16-bit, RLE-garbage and oversized TGAs, a PNG with a lying IHDR, a 0-byte file and JPGs cut short or with a 4096 x 4096 header over one block of scan data (tst_ImageFiles.cpp) LP1c fix (S3.3): a .png or .jpg is dispatched by its content as stbi__load_main dispatches it (M-IMG-DIFF-04) LP1c fix (S2.8): readImageFile and the probe path catch everything, so nothing throws through a copied loader (an allocation failure reads the file as missing); ImageReads begins and ends the image reads and the recording around a load, so they end also when it throws

entries.note: LP1c.2: R_GenerateCubeMapSideFromSingleImage copies a cross of 4 x 3 sides of the cube size out of the picture without looking at the picture's size, so a picture smaller than that is read past its end. Before the copied R_LoadCubeImages runs for a CF_SINGLE image with a cube size, the picture is loaded as it loads it (R_LoadImageProgram, no usage) and a smaller one is refused: the image is the default, with a warning. The picture is decoded twice for such cubes LP1c fix round 2 (X.1): the check now runs inside the transcribed branch (M-IMG-GUARD-04) on the picture the cube is cut from, so the picture is decoded once

LP1c.2: the pre-validation refuses some files the engine would load: images over 16384 a side or 8192 x 8192 in all (the engine has no limit beyond stb_image's 2^24 and the TGA header's 65535), PNG and JPG files cut short that stb_image decodes from zeros, PNG and JPG headers whose size their data cannot hold, unknown critical PNG chunks are refused as stb_image refuses them. An image whose load met a refused file is the default (one warning per refused file, naming it, and not the engine's 'Couldn't load image'), even when R_LoadImage then found another extension of the same name, because the engine would have read past a buffer or crashed on the refused one. LP1c fix (S3.3): the reason "the engine would have read past a buffer or crashed" holds for TGA (Error sites, unchecked RLE), EXR and HDR (Error) only: stb_image checks every read itself and decodes by content, so a .png or .jpg is checked by what it holds (PNG rules for a PNG signature, JPEG rules for a start-of-image marker, stbi_info_from_memory and the size limits for stb_image's other formats), and a refused .png or .jpg is what stb_image's own failure is in the engine: R_LoadImage goes on to the next extension (png, tga, jpg, exr, hdr), and the image is what it finds; a refused TGA, EXR or HDR still makes the image the default. LP1c fix (S2.4): an EXR or HDR file may declare at most a quarter of the pixels (MaxFloatImageFilePixels, 4096 x 4096), as its decoders hold float planes

LP1c.2 (S14): an image's source as ActuallyLoadImage loads it once its cache is not used: the copied R_LoadCubeImages for CF_NATIVE, CF_CAMERA, CF_QUAKE1, CF_SINGLE and CF_PANORAMA (a failure or a side of 0 warns 'Couldn't load cube image: <name>'), the copied R_LoadImageProgram of the PBR-renamed name with the time call's usage for anything else, CF_NATIVE_HDR included as in the engine (a missing picture warns 'Couldn't load image: <name> : <generated name>'); every file through the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01, -02). The pictures are copied out and freed with Mem_Free as ActuallyLoadImage frees them; six sides of 0 that the engine keeps are freed. A quiet load (the editor-image sizes) keeps the copied code's messages in its result. No cache file is written (D11)

entries.note: LP1c.2 (S14, D24, A3): the source fallback. Where the engine would binarize (no cache, or one resolveImageCache calls Stale) the copied loaders read the source (M-IMG-08) and the levels are what Load2DFromMemory or LoadCubeFromMemory hands its encoder with image_highQualityCompression 0: the 2D colour conversion (YCoCg through the copied idColorSpace::ConvertRGBToCoCg_Y for CFM_YCOCG_DXT5; the fast normal-map swizzle x -> alpha, red and blue 0 for CFM_NORMAL_DXT5; alpha -> green for CFM_GREEN_ALPHA), DXT5's colour format forced to CFM_DEFAULT when neither, the mip chain through the copied R_MipMapR11G11B10F (BC6H, R11G11B10F), R_MipMapWithGamma (gammaMips) or R_MipMap, each level stored as the engine stores an uncompressed format (RGB565 high byte first, then expanded with the cache reader's Option 1; LUM8/INT8 red, ALPHA, L8A8, RG16F, R11G11B10F, RGBA8 for anything else) or as the encoder's RGBA8 input (DXT1, DXT5) or R11G11B10F input (BC6H: the SSE build encodes it). A cube: no conversion, CFM_DEFAULT, the records in the engine's images[ level * 6 + side ] order. Format, colour format and gamma mips are DeriveOpts' for the usage the time call found (a program's pixel path may turn the usage TD_BUMP afterwards, which changes nothing, as in the engine); the mip count is DeriveOpts' for the picture's size and the key's filter. The result is a CachedImage tagged fromSource, published in the image's slot; MaterialService::image answers Ready (cache), Source (fallback), Generated (intrinsic) or Default. Differences: M-IMG-DIFF-05. D61 (tst_ImageGoldens.cpp): against the caches the engine wrote for the same sources (capture_fixtures.py's touch material lines; the LP1b caches of its dmap and map), the shape (type, size, levels, records in the engine's order, the stored format and colour layout) is equal for all 17, the RGB565 light image byte for byte, and the DXT1 and DXT5 caches, decoded by the test's BC1 and BC3 decoder, within the bound of the engine's fast encoders (the alpha and the normal map's green fitted alone within range / 16 + range / 6 + quantisation; BC1 colours within the block's range plus quantisation, since the fast encoders never flip the bounding box's diagonal); the HDR panoramas' BC6H caches by their headers and level records (no BC6H decoder)

LP1c.2 (D24, D11): the fallback stops before the encoder: no BC1, BC3 or BC6H on the CPU, so its levels are RGBA8 where the cache holds DXT1 or DXT5 blocks and R11G11B10F where it holds BC6H (the engine accepts R11G11B10F for BC6H, SC99); its 2D levels are unpadded, where the engine pads a DXT level with zeros to whole 4 x 4 blocks, and a cube level below 4 x 4 keeps its size, where the engine replicates it into one block and records 4 x 4. It writes no cache file (the engine binarizes and writes one): the image is made again per session and on a source change. Image arrays and packed mip chains (engine-made bakes) and the editor's own image are never made from a source. LPF.0a (K34): an image override's raw pixels go through the same conversion (sourceLevels, M-FEED-02) and are drawn uncompressed the same way, the feed's normal case, until the file is saved, the engine binarizes it and the override is cleared

entries.note: LP1c.2 (C21, A6, P.4, P.11): MaterialEntry::editorImageSize is GetEditorImage's upload size, measured on the parse thread when the entry is published (sized, LP1b.0's hook), silently (the copied code's messages while it measures are dropped). The chain: qer_editorimage's key as ImageFromFile names and finds it with TF_DEFAULT, TR_REPEAT, TD_DIFFUSE (the default image for an empty or default name, the fonts and lights usages, the extensions stripped, an existing record), without making a record; when its load is defaulted, the first SL_DIFFUSE stage's image or stage 0's when that one has none, but the defaulted editor image when no stage is diffuse; without qer_editorimage the first SL_DIFFUSE stage's image, else stage 0's; no stage or no image: the default image. An image's size: the default image and the fixed-size intrinsics by their generators (16 x 16 for _default, _white, _black, _flat, ...; _quadratic 32 x 4; window-, cvar- and font-sized ones unknown, Default); else the time call names the cache, and a cache the engine would use (not stale, matching DeriveOpts, the BFHACK name too) gives its header's size, read with readGameFileHead (36 bytes, not the body); else the source: a single image's file, the one the copied R_LoadImage's leaf resolution found in the time call (the .tga default, png/tga/jpg/exr/hdr, the _rmao sibling), sized by its header when the loader pre-validation passes it (imageFileHeader); a program or a cube through the copied loaders, quietly (a program by its first leaf; addnormals resamples its second to the first's size); a load that fails or a missing source is the engine's defaulted 8 x 8. Ready is a size the engine uploads; Default is the defaulted 8 x 8 or an unknown size, with the reason. A Ready size is kept per canonical name across reloads (D52). The LP1b fixture's six editor images equal the engine's listImages, from the caches' headers and from the sources' alike (tst_EditorImageSize.cpp)

LP1c.2 (C21): the engine loads an image once per level and again on reloadImages; the preview re-reads on its 1 s poll: the loose files each published editor-image size and each image slot was read from, or that the time call found, are probed (no body read), and one whose time, size or change stamp changed makes the slot read again (resolveImage) and the material's size measured again, its kept Ready size dropped so that the new size or the loss of the file is published under every name that shares the entry. Files in containers are not polled (their tables are read once). A Ready size that changes to another Ready size reaches the chunks only when they are rebuilt for another reason: SceneGeometry rebuilds provisional (Default) chunks when their size turns Ready (a follow-up) LP1c fix (S2.5, S2.7): SceneGeometry keeps the size each material's cells were built with and builds them again on any change of the table's size (Default to Ready, Ready to another Ready, Ready back to Default for a deleted texture); the poll re-probes a slice of at most 5 ms per poll, going on where it stopped, with stop checks; a measure that the poll asks for is queued (M-IMG-DIFF-08)

LP1c.2 (C21): a single source image is sized by its header, never decoded: a file that passes the loader pre-validation but that stb_image or tinyexr then fails to decode (corrupt compressed data) is Ready at its header's size here and the engine's defaulted 8 x 8 there. An intrinsic the engine sizes by its window, a cvar or a font atlas (_currentRender, _shadowMapAtlas, _imguiFont, ...) is Default here. GetEditorImage's record is never made, so listImages-like listings of the registry do not show editor images the engine's dmap would have loaded LP1c fix (S2.2, S3.3): every source size is a header's now (M-IMG-DIFF-08), a program's by its first leaf and a cube's by its sides' headers; a .png or .jpg whose header is refused gives way to the next extension's file, as the engine's loop does

entries.note: LP1c fix (S2.1): when R_LoadCubeImages stops at side i (a side missing, which leaves width 0, or of another size) it frees sides 0 to i-1 without nulling them and returns false; a side i it loaded before the size test failed is leaked (the engine's ActuallyLoadImage frees nothing after the false). Kept verbatim (C7). The shim frees nothing after a false return (LP1c.2 freed every non-null side again: a double free, S2.1/S3.1) and frees the six sides only for a loaded cube of size 0; the six sides' headers are checked first (M-IMG-GUARD-03), so the copy is called only for six sides of one size and the leak is unreachable; a side refused by the pre-validation as the copy reads it, or a stop between sides, reads as missing, and the copy frees what it loaded itself LP1c fix round 2 (X.2): the header check does not make the leak unreachable by itself: a side 0 whose header passes but whose body is refused or does not decode leaves width 0, side 1 then fails the size test and is leaked. So side 0 is also decoded whole (the copied R_LoadImageProgram, inside the image reads) before the copy runs, and a side 0 without a picture fails the load; the leak is unreachable unless a side changes on disk between that decode and the copy's LP1c fix round 3 (Y.1): that, too, was not the whole truth: a side's load can find another file than the one whose header was checked (a refused .tga, then a sibling .png of another size), and side 0 decoded alone compared no size. So the pixel path no longer calls the copied loop: the shim runs a transcription of R_LoadCubeImages' six-file part (loadSixFileCube) that also frees the side that stops the loop on its size, and the leak is unreachable on every path. The side-0 decode of round 2 is gone (side 0 is decoded once again); the copy keeps the defect verbatim and runs only for the time call

LP1c fix (S2.1, S2.2): before the copied R_LoadCubeImages reads a six-file cube's pixels (CF_NATIVE, CF_CAMERA, CF_QUAKE1, CF_SINGLE without a cube size), each side's name (R_LoadCubeImages' side tables, transcribed) is resolved by the copied time call (R_LoadImageProgram, no pixels) and its file's header read through the source without its body: a side missing, a header refused or sides of different sizes (side 0 square) fail the load with "Couldn't load cube image" (and the engine's "Mismatched sizes on cube map" for sizes) without the copy. The same check sizes a cube for C21 (side 0's header) without decoding it LP1c fix round 2: side 0 is decoded whole before the copy (X.2, M-IMG-DEFECT-03), and a side whose .png or .jpg header is refused gives way to the next extension of the loader order, as R_LoadImage does after stb_image's failure (X.9) LP1c fix round 3 (Y.1): the header check is now an early refusal (and C21's sizing); the guard against the leak is the transcribed loop (loadSixFileCube), which frees every side it loaded when it fails, the mismatched one included

LP1c fix (S2.2): the engine sizes an editor image when dmap loads it; the preview publishes a material at once with its last Ready size for the same image chain (D52, S3.15) or the registry's Default, unmeasured, and measures it on a low-priority queue (steps of 20 ms) only once a consumer looked it up (the bulk parse measures nothing; a lookup of a bulk-parsed name queues it). The measure never decodes: a usable cache's 36-byte header; else a 2D image or program by its first leaf's header, once the time call found every leaf (a missing leaf ends the copied time call, so its last probe is a miss); a six-file cube by side 0 after M-IMG-GUARD-03; a CF_SINGLE cube by its cube size once the picture's header holds the 4 x 3 sides; a panorama 1024. Headers come through small bounded reads (4 KB, 64 KB, 1 MB; readImageFileHeader), with the header rules and the lengths a header tells; the body of a file (RLE packets, PNG chunks, JPEG scans, EXR blocks) is not walked, so a file the pre-validation refuses by its body has a Ready size here (M-IMG-DIFF-07). A kept Ready size stands for a Default measure only while the files it was measured from are unchanged; a deleted texture returns to Default

LP1c fix (S2.3, S2.4, S2.5): the engine keeps an image in VRAM once loaded; the preview's parse thread reads images in work items of up to 100 ms (or 256 images; LP4.3: a read batch's containers are reopened per item), each ending after the image in hand once more urgent work is queued (a reload, an evaluation, an image override (LPF.0a), a lookup, a bake, a measure), below the lookups, the measures and the evaluations, and keeps the published images' data within MaterialServiceOptions::imageBudgetBytes (512 MB): beyond it, the least recently published image whose data a consumer has taken (image() returned it) leaves the table and is read again when asked for (about 0.5 ms a cache). A reload drops the image slots whose files changed (LP1c fix round 2, below), so new containers and caches the engine wrote are seen then (materialCollectionsDidChange, or a new session). The source fallback takes the loader's pixels as its working buffer and writes its levels into one buffer reserved for them all (about 1.3 GB less for an 8192 x 8192 source); it stops between levels once the session stops. LP2's upload-and-drop policy and the VRAM budget are LP2's LP1c fix round 2 (X.3): a reload drops only the image slots whose files the new source finds otherwise (a file found or missed, the cache's name included, a container entry's kind and container) and slots with no file; an unchanged slot keeps its pointer, so an .mtr save reads no image again. (X.11) A slot the poll drops is no longer counted as taken. (X.4, recorded) An evaluation waits at most for the work item in flight, which is one image (the batch ends after it) or one bake: a source decode costs about 39 ms per 1024 x 1024 PNG in Release (the retail materialorb sources), so up to about 2.5 s at the 8192 x 8192 cap (D51), more in Debug; LP2's requests should ask small images first or bound a decode per item

LP1c fix (S2.2): the engine opens a loose file by trying it; the preview lists each loose folder it looks in once and keeps its names (folded as the file system compares them), so a file that is not there costs a lookup, not a file-system call. looseFilesMayHaveChanged (the parse thread's 1 s poll) starts a round: the first look into a folder after it stats the folder and lists it again when its time changed. A file added after its folder was listed is seen at the next poll (the poll's re-probe then reads what missed it again, M-IMG-DIFF-03); a changed file is seen by its own stat as before. A .resources container is statted once when a read batch opens it, not per read: a container replaced during one batch is read through the handle the batch opened, and refused from the next LP1c fix round 2 (X.10): a folder whose time is within 2 s of its listing is listed again at each new round, so a file added within the same tick of a coarse file-system clock (FAT, exFAT, HFS+, some network shares) is not missed LP1c fix round 3 (Y.3): a folder whose time lies ahead of the clock (a share's skew) is not "recent": it is listed once, and again only when its time changes

entries.note: K28 (31-LP2-FIXES.md, replacing DX.1; restated in round 2 from 32-LP2-VERIFY.md V2.1): dmap runs OptimizeEntity on every area by default, which throws away each coplanar group's side triangles and builds them again (BuildOptTriangles, RegenerateTriangles) from candidate edges sorted by an unstable qsort (equal lengths tie, as a rectangle's two diagonals do), so the .proc's triangles are not fans of the side windings (the parity .proc: 96 of 110 pairs of the (a b c)(d c b) shape); copying the optimizer would import the CRT's qsort tie order. The preview keeps its own triangulation (K9's family). The mechanism by which this changes pixels: the interaction vertex shader writes the normalised vector to the viewer per vertex in tangent space (interaction.vs.hlsl:193-200), the rasteriser interpolates it over the triangle, and the pixel shader normalises it again (interaction.ps.hlsl:98) and reads it in the view-dependent normal contrast before the Lambert term (:112-121) and in the half vector and the BRDF (:138-139, :181-183). A per-vertex normalised vector interpolated over a triangle depends on the triangle: the same face cut along the other diagonal gives another per-pixel view vector (4-17 degrees apart on large triangles near the camera, measured from the .proc's triangles). So bump-mapped and specular pixels differ wherever a triangle is large against its distance from the camera: |d| <= 4 on R05 (941 pixels beyond 1), <= 2 on R18 (28), masked <= 17 at texel edges on R08, R09 and R12's ceilings, |d| = 1 on 0.01-3 % of every bump-mapped row, and up to 12 where a triangle crosses the near plane (R05b: 2,568 unmasked pixels from 2 to 12, 9,950 at 1, masked max 7; the same on the LP2.3 run and the fix round's). A flat normal and no specular stage do not take the view vector out (V3.1, 32-LP2-VERIFY.md, corrected in LP4.1): without a specular stage the engine zeroes the specular colour (RenderBackend.cpp:2151 clears inter.specularColor, :1156-1158 binds _black for a missing specular image, :1190 writes the zero SPECULARMODIFIER), so the BRDF's specular term and its Fresnel_Schlick( 0, vdotH ) contribute nothing; the view vector reaches these pixels through the view-dependent normal contrast (interaction.ps.hlsl:112-121), which scales the decoded normal's xy by 0.8-1.2 with the per-pixel view vector's z, and _flat does not decode to exactly (0, 0) (about (0.0020, 0.0033): DXT5 alpha 128 and green 128 1/3), so the tilt of the normal, and with it the Lambert term, follows the interpolated view vector. Round 2's R19-R21 (R01-R03's lights on legacy diffuse with bumpmap _flat) differ by 1 on 1,677, 355 and 957 unmasked pixels, mostly on the large floor and ceiling triangles; R14 is exact because its parallel light meets the wall head-on (L near N), where the Lambert term does not feel so small a tilt, not because the wall is uniform. Near-plane clipping only amplifies the effect (a vertex beside or behind the camera carries a view vector almost perpendicular to the view); the parity rows' room split 100 units ahead of the camera (parity.py room_split) stays, harmless. The parity method: R05, R18 and R19-R21 are K28 rows with recorded thresholds (max, mean, p99, the count beyond 1; the mean pins a row's |d| = 1 count), R14 the exact row, the other axial rows +-1 (K28's empirical bound there), R05b reported; the classes live in parity.py's row table. LP7 (a follow-up, not done): draw the .proc's triangles in the parity path, test-only first, then for the faces unchanged since the bake. Also seen on the fix round's run: dmap snaps brush vertices to its 1/32 grid and removes the faces that lie in slabs thinner than 0.1 between near-coplanar planes (a wall behind panels 0.05 in front of it), and an entity inside such a slab is linked to no area; the preview builds the editor's brushes as they are, so faces closer than 0.1 to another brush's parallel plane can differ in the same way (R13 is built without such faces since round 2).

The render thread asks for every area's atlas when it adopts a table (also the areas without points, as LoadLightGridImages does); an area with points whose atlas is Pending keeps the frame unconverged (FrameConvergence::gridImagesPending: the engine loads them at map load). The points themselves are read (M-BAKE-03) and only counted
